cases.title: Scan recently changed files for all intent clarity issues
cases.user_request: Run an intent clarity audit on files changed in the last 14 days. Check all five categories and show me the top 25 findings.

notes: Recent commits include files with nested ternaries, single-letter variable names in long functions, and bare boolean arguments.
Some files use idiomatic short variable names in loops that should not be flagged.

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with findings grouped by severity
Each finding includes category, file:line, code snippet, and explanation
Summary with category breakdown and hotspot files
static_checks: All referenced files appear in git log for the last 14 days
Findings are grouped into high, medium, and low severity sections
Every snippet is real code from the referenced file and line
review_questions: Are severity assignments consistent with the skill's classification criteria?
Are idiomatic patterns (loop variables, unused-var underscores) correctly excluded from findings?

cases.title: Restrict scan to nested ternaries and unnamed booleans only
cases.user_request: Run an intent clarity audit but only check for nested ternaries and unnamed boolean parameters. Skip the other three categories. Scan the full repo, not just recent changes.

notes: User wants only two of five categories.
Findings from unclear names, clever one-liners, and restating comments should not appear.

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with only nested-ternary and unnamed-boolean findings
No findings from the other three categories
Report notes which categories were enabled
static_checks: No finding has a category outside of 'Nested ternary' or 'Unnamed boolean'
Report header or notes mention the category filter
review_questions: Did the agent correctly limit findings to only the two requested categories?
Are the nested ternary and unnamed boolean findings themselves accurate and well-classified?

cases.title: Idiomatic patterns are not flagged as false positives
cases.user_request: Run an intent clarity audit on this repository. I want to make sure it does not flag idiomatic patterns like loop index variables, Python underscore conventions, or standard short names in list comprehensions.

notes: Repository contains Python list comprehensions with single-letter variables.
Go code uses short receiver names (idiomatic).
JavaScript code uses `_` for unused callback parameters.
These are all idiomatic and should not be flagged.

artifact_requirements: Markdown report that does not flag idiomatic short names
If any idiomatic patterns are noted, they are marked as excluded rather than findings
Findings focus on genuinely unclear code, not language conventions
static_checks: No finding flags a single-letter loop index in a loop body of 5 lines or fewer
No finding flags underscore-prefixed unused variables
No finding flags Go single-letter receiver names
review_questions: Does the report correctly distinguish idiomatic short names from genuinely unclear names?
Are there any false positives where a language-standard convention was flagged?
